answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks using hardware-rooted remote attestation. Agents execute inside trusted enclaves, turning each runtime into an oasis of tamper-proof computation. This forces an attacker to incur the verifiable capital cost of procuring scarce physical silicon per identity. While this stops botnets from draining reward nectar via cheap virtual personas, it restricts participation to a vendor-controlled hardware horizon vulnerable to side-channel key extraction.
